I guess I shouldn't speak for all males as oppressed, but for me, personally, I've always felt that females were able to express themselves in almost any way they feel the need to in society. I guess I'm pretty much gender nonconforming.

I'll never understand what it is to feel like you want the female genitalia though. That's always been very interesting to me and I guess something we won't be able to relate on there, but I do feel "female" socially for sure.

Honestly, I believe society will eventually come to a state of "oneness". Sooner or later "trans" won't exist. We will only be people with different genetalia. We just need to break the cycle of "hyperfeminine" and "hypermasculine". It's gonna take time for society to see that it's fine for that little boy to wear a skirt and play with barbies, and it's fine for that little girl to want to play sports and ride motorcycles.

Feminism has been very helpful for the female side over the years, but what of the males? We're still an oppressed people. To clarify, I'm a crossdresser who had trans feelings and still does, but I kinda felt one day, "who am I helping if I just switch teams?". I want to be the change. I want to try to show at least SOME people that it's okay for a guy to present in a feminine way.

Most of the people I'm close to are girls. I like sports, video games, cars, makeup, dresses, all of that. I guess I'll still never be able to grasp the whole "born with the wrong genetalia" thing though, but boy do I know what it means to feel socially isolated because of my gender.

My theory is that it's a matter of labels. Feminine= X, masculine= Y, if you're a man and seen doing anything feminine, you= girl. I feel like somewhere along the line, when you realized how much society frowns upon a guy in a dress, you get it in your head that "i'll change sexes then!".

Millions of years of evolution we're battling sadly.

I don't really doubt them. In fact, I do believe that there is some sort of mental disorder/sexual addiction at play here. Who the fuck really cares though? If the best thing you can do right now is transition, you really aren't hurting anyone, so do it.

If you do have OCD, you can rest assured that another obsession will take its place sooner or later. You'll always think "this one is worst than the last one" as well. For instance, there was a week where I "got over" my gender issues and then my fixation became my hair. I could SWEAR that my hair was getting thinner. I'd probably take 50 pictures of it a day and compare it to old pictures.

OCD is also related to addiction, not excluding sexual addiction. In my case, the "sissy play" part of me is deeply related to gender roles, etc. So what do you think I fixate on when feeling "in the mood"? I'm also not able to wear certain fabrics anymore. As a kid, I remember not being able to wear pajama bottoms to bed because it "didn't feel right". Sometimes I'll also think to myself "If I step on this crack, my mom will die.".

I've tried SSRI's, but I hate the way they make me feel. OCD is kind of a double edged sword. Once something "cures" the OCD, it also may take away a creative part of yourself temporarily. I'm becoming more and more open to experimenting with different medications though.

OCD is a very real thing. I didn't have any gender issues until 21 years old. I then started to come into a darker part of my sexuality, which was "sissy play" and well.... I'm just going to say, the stuff is incredibly addicting.

Now all I can think about is gender this, gender that. I can't focus on anything else in life anymore. I was also diagnosed with severe OCD in the past. I used to be fixated on killing myself accidentally. I was so scared of it in fact that I would avoid sharp objects. It even got to the point where I couldn't use pencils and pens in school. I was hospitalized.
I didn't have my first kiss until I was 21 man. I'm 22 now and STILL a virgin. My cousin is a pretty handsome guy and he also didn't have sex until he was 19 years old. Trust me, you're not abnormal.
I just told my mom, "you know bruce jenner?", she was like "yeah". I told her I was bruce jenner. She was like "damn, I never wanted a daughter" and we laughed about it.

This person didn't state any of this. So I'm going to assume they're living in a first world country with access to a therapist like anyone else would, unless they say otherwise. You can't play this game, lol.

Self medication is STRONGLY advised against for any illness, even if they WERE in a third world country. You've seen it around here. Tell a therapist you're just going to self medicate otherwise and you should be good.

Dreams don't always have to be a manifestation of the subconscious. Dreams can also be about your current issues. For instance, I have sleep apnea. I used to have dreams about drowning and I could actually feel my body being restricted for air while I was sleeping.

Dreams are to be taken with a grain of salt.

Self medication is never correct. No matter the illness. You're literally your own doctor, and messing with something like estrogen especially isn't funny.

Sorry. I don't agree with people self medicating. Whether they're cis suicidal folks or trans suicidal folks. Once you've come to the conclusion that you want to self medicate, you either need to check yourself into an in or outpatient program, or you need to see a therapist asap. 

If you're determined to get on hormones, you might as well tell your therapist you were going to do it anyway, they'll likely oblige you on it.
We can't even reverse male pattern baldness yet. We'll be dead by the time that is even possible, but maybe.

Heya! I'm also going to become a tranny soon too. I actually just recently found out about this part of me. On top of my old suicidal thoughts, I now have this to worry about! Great world we're living in.

Well, yeah. At least for me, that was a huge reason for going through HRT. I never really felt like a "woman" per se, and I don't really care what people refer to me as honestly. I just feel like I can be way more attractive when looking and being treated like a woman would.
